analysis.investment_thesis: Meesho fails every quantitative test I require: three consecutive years of losses, a P/B of 50x, and equity being destroyed at an accelerating pace (-₹3,942 Cr net loss in FY2025 versus -₹328 Cr the prior year). At ₹74,700 Cr market cap against ₹1,446 Cr of book equity, Mr. Market is paying 51 times net assets for a business that has never earned a rupee of profit.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at ~28% CAGR (₹5,735→₹9,390 Cr) — the business is gaining scale
Operating cash flow turned positive in FY2024 and FY2025 (₹220 Cr, ₹539 Cr) — suggests improving unit economics at the operating level
Debt is negligible (D/E 0.09, borrowings ₹58 Cr) — no near-term solvency risk from leverage
key_risks: Accelerating net losses — FY2025 loss of ₹3,942 Cr is 12x the FY2024 loss of ₹328 Cr, with other income collapsing to -₹835 Cr
Book equity eroding rapidly: ₹2,472 Cr → ₹1,446 Cr in two years; at this pace, equity is destroyed entirely within two more years without fresh capital
P/B of 50.42 offers zero margin of safety — Graham Number is incalculable given negative earnings; intrinsic value cannot be established
red_flags: Zero earnings history across all three available years — fails my minimum 3-5 year positive earnings requirement absolutely
FY2025 other income of -₹835 Cr (vs +₹231 Cr in FY2024) suggests significant hidden investment losses or write-downs
Promoter holding of only 16.57% — founders and early backers have distributed risk widely; insiders do not stand behind this business with their own capital
Investing cash outflow of ₹2,638 Cr in FY2025 financed by ₹2,105 Cr in financing activities — perpetual capital consumer with no demonstrated path to self-sufficiency
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Meesho is a textbook speculative growth story of the kind I have warned investors against throughout my career. The stock trades at 50x book value and 6.5x revenues for a business that has never produced a single year of profit. My Graham Number requires both positive earnings and positive book value — Meesho satisfies neither condition. The FY2025 net loss explosion to ₹3,942 Cr (versus ₹328 Cr in FY2024) is deeply alarming; stripping out the collapse in other income (likely unrealised investment losses), the operating business itself lost ₹578 Cr at the operating income line. Equity has been consumed from ₹2,472 Cr to ₹1,446 Cr in just two years.

The one concession I will grant is that operating cash flow has turned positive (₹539 Cr in FY2025), and the balance sheet carries almost no financial debt. But these are table stakes, not investment merits. The market is pricing in a future that has not been earned and may never arrive. I require a margin of safety — a discount to demonstrated, proven intrinsic value. Here, there is no intrinsic value to discount from. An intelligent investor does not speculate on what a business might become; he buys what a business demonstrably is. Meesho, at ₹164, is a speculation dressed in the language of commerce.
